title: Why Do Phantom Traffic Jams Happen?
description:
No crash. No roadwork. So why did you just sit in traffic for 20 minutes?
In 2008, researchers put 22 cars on an empty circle and asked them to drive at a steady 30 km/h. Within minutes, a traffic jam appeared out of nothing. Here's why it happens, why the jam moves backward, and what one calm car (and 100 automated vehicles on a real highway) can do about it.

All 3D scenes are simulations or illustrations based on the sources below.

0:00 A jam with no cause
0:14 The 2008 circle experiment
1:08 Why it happens: a small delay, repeated
2:31 The jam moves backward
3:17 Phantom jams on real highways
4:10 "Jamitons" (MIT, 2009)
4:59 One calm car (2018)
5:43 100 automated cars on I-24 (2022)
6:31 Two ways to fight the waves
7:44 What you can do
8:37 Nobody crashed

Sources
- Sugiyama et al. (2008), "Traffic jams without bottlenecks", New Journal of Physics 10, 033001

- Stern et al. (2018), Transportation Research Part C 89, 205–221 (arXiv 1705.01693)
- Review of variable speed limits and jam-absorption driving, arXiv 2504.11372 (2025)
- FHWA-HRT-06-033, Appendix A (perceptual-motor reaction time, citing Green 2000)
